# Code of conduct

## Our standard

This project is a technical one. Everyone taking part — reporting issues, sending pull requests, reviewing, or discussing — is expected to be respectful and constructive, to accept technical criticism of their work, and to keep discussion on the engineering question at hand.

Unacceptable behavior includes personal attacks, harassment of any kind, publishing others' private information, and deliberately derailing technical discussion. Sustained disruption after a warning is also unacceptable.

## Honesty about results

This project's review culture depends on accurate claims. Do not report checks as executed when they were configured, skipped or unavailable, and do not present generated or assumed output as measured results. State plainly what ran, on what platform, and what did not. See [CONTRIBUTING](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Handling documents and reports

Issues and pull requests are public. Never attach real documents containing personal, medical, financial or otherwise sensitive content; use the synthetic fixtures the tests provide, or describe reproduction steps without the source material. Suspected vulnerabilities follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) instead of public issues.

## Enforcement

The maintainer, Ervins Strauhmanis, is responsible for this standard and may edit, hide or remove contributions that violate it, and may block accounts that continue after a warning. Concerns can be raised privately through the repository's private reporting channels; reports are handled as confidentially as the platform allows.

This code of conduct applies in the repository and in any project space where someone represents the project.
